title: Changelog governance and stakeholder onboarding
creator: Ava Chen
summary: Create a repeatable governance process and onboarding playbook for drafting, reviewing, redacting, and publishing product changelogs (internal and customer-facing). Goal is to reduce last-minute signoff bottlenecks and ensure consistent messaging across teams.
background: Multiple launches in the last 6 months exposed gaps: inconsistent changelog tone, variable redaction practices, and unclear owner handoffs. PMs currently chase reviews across Slack and email which delays publish windows. This initiative centralizes the process and provides a lightweight governance model and templates.
objectives: Define a 3-step review flow (Draft -> Technical Review -> Comms Signoff) with SLAs
Ship a changelog template for internal + customer-facing entries (includes impact, mitigation, and opt-out guidance)
Create an onboarding checklist for cross-functional owners (Eng, Design, Legal, Support, Growth)
Automate notification to reviewers via Slack/GitHub when drafts are ready
Document redaction policy and maintain a minimal PII checklist
scope: All public changelogs associated with console and API releases
Internal release digest for Customer Success and Sales
Owner rotation and escalation paths for signoff
out_of_scope: Localization translation execution (we will hand off to localization team after signoff)
Automated publishing to external marketplaces (separate pipeline)
Full editorial rewrite of older changelog archives
deliverables: Changelog governance doc (Confluence): process, SLAs, owners
Customer-facing changelog template (Google Doc) + internal digest template
Signoff checklist and automated reviewer Slack workflow
Owner onboarding playbook and 30-minute training deck
Redaction/PII checklist and legal FAQ stub

signoff_criteria: Technical accuracy confirmed by owner in ENG within 48 hours
Legal redaction checklist reviewed and cleared (if required)
Communications approves tone and customer impact language
CS and Sales receive internal digest and confirm no missing customer blockers
All required fields in the template are filled and linked to PRs/dashboards
review_process: Draft author creates Google Doc using the customer-facing template
Ping reviewers via #changelog-review Slack and include links to PRs and dashboards
Technical reviewers annotate the draft and add an explicit accept/reject comment
Legal flags any PII or contractual language using the PII checklist
Final comms signoff happens in the Signoff column in the release board
templates: Customer-facing changelog snippet: 'What changed', 'Who it affects', 'Mitigation/Workarounds', 'Rollout/How to opt-out', 'Link to more details'
Internal digest fields: 'Impact level', 'Customer-facing excerpt', 'Key commits/PRs', 'CS talking points'
localization_plan: Mark entries that require translation at signoff using 'translate: yes' label
Send finalized copy to Localization queue within 24 hours of signoff
Localization to provide target-language drafts within 3 business days for priority launches
risks: Late technical changes that invalidate approved text
Reviewer SLAs not met leading to missed publish windows
Conflicting messaging across channels (console vs blog vs email)
mitigation: Freeze window for content edits 24 hours before publish; any post-freeze edits require fast-track approval
Maintain a rolling roster of backup reviewers and escalate to Eng manager after 24 hours
Use the PII checklist and require Legal signoff for anything mentioning customer names or data
Add a 'single source of truth' link to the changelog entry that other channels must reference
